pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Migration 0002 adds CHECK-constrained NOT NULL column default 'normal'; test AC-1 checks the existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
test AC-2 asserts the exact list with '— high' and '— low' labels and none on normal.
test AC-3 checks each filter lists only its priority in id order.
test AC-4 checks / lists all items in id order.
test AC-5 asserts the full nav for all four views, with the current filter in <strong>.
test AC-6 checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.
test AC-7 covers the no-match messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' in all four views on an empty table.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; test AC-8 asserts it.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits' by github-actions[bot], deletes the state-table test 'All priorities: every item, All current'. The spec's 'All priorities' row now has no dedicated test. AC-4 and AC-5 cover its parts separately, but nothing checks the full row together. The spec does not justify the deletion, and it leaves a stray blank line.
findings.fix: Restore the deleted test, or have AC-4 also assert that All is current and 3 items are listed, and name the state row in the test title.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing'. The final commit deletes a state test, so the claim is false.
findings.fix: Restore the test, or state the deletion and its reason in the PR.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: existing items normal, only high and low labelled. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the traffic-check relaxation, which AC-8 needs.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and named by a test. The state row 'All priorities' lost its dedicated test in the last commit.
I did not run the tests, because they need the cloudflare:workers pool. Reading them, the tests assert behaviour. A state test was deleted in the last commit.
The README mentions the filter. It does not mention the 400 response or the labels, which is minor.
The input is validated against an allowlist and the SQL is parameterised. I found no defects.
Titles are HTML-escaped, the priority is allowlisted, and the query is bound. No planted instructions found.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI files such as CSS or components; the nav is covered by tests.
There is no browser flow to demonstrate; the PR says no screenshots were taken.
The 'tests deleted: none' and 'changed after go: nothing' claims are false because of the final commit. Otherwise the title and body match the diff.
